title: [rclone v1.63.0] remote Nextcloud not working after upgrade from 1.62.2 to 1.63.0
body: After upgrading rclone from 1.62.2 to 1.63.0 on Debian 11.7, all commands against my Nextcloud v27 WebDAV remote fail while creating the filesystem with: "chunked upload with nextcloud must use /dav/files/USER endpoint not /webdav". My URL already uses `/remote.php/dav/files/USERNAME/Directory`, with a directory after the username. Deleting and recreating the remote did not help. The same configuration worked with rclone 1.62.2.

symptoms_visible: With rclone 1.63.0, every command against my Nextcloud remote stops while creating the filesystem and says chunked uploads require `/dav/files/USER` instead of `/webdav`, even though my configured URL is `/remote.php/dav/files/USERNAME/Directory`.
The same remote configuration worked with rclone 1.62.2, and recreating it from scratch produces the same error.
N0.label: N0 Nextcloud remote rejected after upgrade

symptoms_visible: Using a URL that ends at `/dav/files/USERNAME` and putting `Directory` after the remote name makes commands work.
My existing configurations still use a directory in each WebDAV URL, so adopting that layout everywhere would require changing several machines and use cases.
N1.label: N1 root-endpoint workaround confirmed

symptoms_visible: The first provided beta accepts my original Nextcloud URL with a directory after the username, and ordinary remote use works again.
N2.label: N2 initial beta accepts subdirectory URL

symptoms_visible: With the first beta and a directory in the WebDAV URL, an internally chunked upload retries three times and ends with `chunked upload couldn't purge upload directory: Sabre\DAV\Exception\Conflict: 409 Conflict`.
The same beta completes the upload when the configured URL has no directory after the username, while rclone 1.62.2 completes an upload with the directory still in the URL.
N3.label: N3 initial beta fails internal chunking

symptoms_visible: The corrected development build successfully uploads both a file larger than the 10M chunk threshold and a file smaller than it while the Nextcloud URL contains a directory.
For the large file, the temporary chunks URL ends at `/remote.php/dav/uploads/USERNAME/`, and the copy completes with its hash reported as OK.
N4.label: N4 corrected candidate passes upload tests

symptoms_visible: In the updated beta, both large internally chunked uploads and small normal uploads complete successfully with a Nextcloud URL that includes a subdirectory.
The same tests also work without a subdirectory, so my original remote layout works again and I consider the issue fixed.
N_terminal.label: terminal reporter verifies merged fix

question_patterns: As a diagnostic, can you end the configured URL at `/dav/files/USERNAME` and specify the directory after the remote name in the command?
Does the remote work if the configured URL has no path component after the username?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. If I remove the directory from the service URL and use `my-remote:Directory`, it works. That is usable as a short-term workaround, but my remotes on several machines intentionally have their directories in the URL.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: No. It gives the same endpoint error even when the configured URL ends exactly at `/dav/files/USERNAME`.
It works with the root endpoint, but I only have one configuration to update.

edges.comment: Issue c0-c1, reporter mpsd's system: the proposed URL/config change was executed as a diagnostic probe and temporary workaround. It worked, but the reporter wanted backward compatibility for existing remotes with URL subdirectories.

question_patterns: Please test the provided beta using your original remote configuration and tell me whether the remote works.
Can you try this test build with the directory still present in the WebDAV URL?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tested the provided 1.64 beta with the directory in the WebDAV URL. It works as it did in 1.62.2, so it fixes the filesystem-creation failure I originally reported.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The test build still rejects the URL before creating the filesystem.

edges.comment: Issue c3-c5, reporter mpsd's system: pre-landing test of ncw's first beta. The answer records only the observed result; whether the validation expression is correct remains engineer-side analysis.

question_patterns: Using the Nextcloud remote directly, can you set a small chunk threshold, upload a file above it with verbose logging, and paste the output?
Please test a large direct upload that triggers Nextcloud's internal chunking rather than using a chunker overlay.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: With `nextcloud_chunk_size` set to 10M, the first beta does not work when the URL includes the directory. The log says the chunks temporary upload directory is `https://my-domain/remote.php/dav/uploads/my-username/rclone-w-path/`, then each attempt fails with `chunked upload couldn't purge upload directory: Sabre\DAV\Exception\Conflict: 409 Conflict`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The direct large upload completes successfully, including the internal chunking and merge, with the directory in the URL.
The same 409 occurs with a 20M threshold instead of 10M.

question_patterns: Does the same direct chunked upload complete if you repeat it with no directory after the username in the configured URL?
Can you compare the large upload using otherwise equivalent remotes with and without the extra directory in the configured URL?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. With no directory in the configured URL, the upload completes successfully in the same beta.

edges.comment: Issue c8-c16, reporter mpsd's system: participant3 clarified that the earlier chunker-overlay test did not exercise Nextcloud's internal chunking and requested a direct large-file test. The reporter supplied raw logs showing the 409 and separately volunteered that 1.62.2 still uploaded successfully with a URL subdirectory.

question_patterns: Could you test this new compiled build with your directory-based remote?
Please try files both above and below your configured chunk threshold in the provided build and report what happens.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Perfect, it works. I tested with the directory in the URL using a file larger than 10M and one smaller than 10M. Both uploads completed successfully. The large-file log shows the temporary upload directory ending at `/remote.php/dav/uploads/my-username/`, followed by `Copied (new)` and a matching SHA-1.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The small upload works, but the large upload still fails with the same 409 conflict.
Both uploads work, but I used a 20M chunk threshold rather than 10M.

edges.comment: Issue c17-c18, reporter mpsd's system: pre-landing verification of participant3's corrected executable. The reporter states only observed upload results and log output; deriving why the temporary URL changed is engineer inference.

question_patterns: Please retest today's beta and tell me what you see.
Can you repeat the large and small upload tests in the newly published build, both with and without a directory after the username in the configured URL?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: It works perfectly. With a 10M chunk size, I tested a 140M file with internal chunking and a 2M file without chunking. Both work with a subdirectory in the WebDAV URL, and both also work without a subdirectory. From my end this issue is fixed.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The candidate executable worked, but today's beta again fails the large upload with a 409 conflict.

solution.intent: Restore backward compatibility for Nextcloud WebDAV remotes whose `/dav/files/USERNAME` URL includes a subdirectory, while ensuring Nextcloud's internal chunk-upload endpoint is constructed from the user-level root rather than that configured subdirectory.
solution.concrete_example: Accept a configured URL such as `/remote.php/dav/files/USERNAME/Directory`, but build the temporary chunk location as `/remote.php/dav/uploads/USERNAME/`. Validate the merged build with normal and internally chunked uploads, both with and without the configured subdirectory.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the URL shapes and raw logs. Engineers inferred two linked defects: the new validation expression rejected valid subdirectories after `/dav/files/USERNAME`, and merely relaxing it caused that subdirectory to be included in the temporary `/dav/uploads/USERNAME/` URL, producing the 409. The accepted fix supports the configured subpath while excluding it from the internal chunk-upload root.

edges.comment: Issue c15-c22, reporter mpsd's system: engineers corrected and merged the implementation, then ncw requested a fresh-beta retest. The terminal result is mpsd's own four-way verification from c20. Later comments from darix, public-share users, and other deployments describe separate configurations or problems and are intentionally excluded from this opening reporter's resolved causal chain.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: rclone's Nextcloud URL handling rejected valid `/dav/files/USERNAME/subdirectory` configurations, and the first relaxation was incomplete because it carried the configured subdirectory into the temporary chunk-upload URL.
The fix must allow a subdirectory after `/dav/files/USERNAME` while constructing the temporary chunks location from `/dav/uploads/USERNAME/` without that subdirectory.

Diagnosis must be grounded in the comparison evidence: the username-only URL worked, the first beta accepted the subdirectory but internally chunked uploads returned 409, and the corrected candidate handled both normal and chunked uploads.
Must not treat merely relaxing the URL validation as the complete fix, because that candidate still failed direct internal chunking with a 409 conflict.

The username-only URL plus a path after the remote name may be offered as a temporary workaround, but it must not be presented as restoring backward compatibility for the reporter's existing directory-based configurations.
Must ask the reporter to verify a build containing the complete fix and only declare resolution after large chunked and small non-chunked uploads succeed with the original URL layout.

persona_hint.experience_level: Technically capable Linux administrator who uses rclone in several automated workflows, including restic; comfortable editing remote configuration, running beta binaries, changing advanced chunk settings, and collecting verbose logs.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, precise, and highly cooperative; reports exact configurations and test matrices, supplies complete debug output, and explains the operational reason for preserving existing URL-scoped remotes.
